title: Roberto Vercellino
text:
Professional Summary

Energy systems research engineer and quantitative analyst with 5 years of experience developing decision-support models, optimization software, and techno-economic analyses to guide infrastructure and investment decisions for government agencies, utilities, and industry partners.
Specialized in energy and power systems modeling, mathematical optimization, HPC-scale simulation, and financial/techno-economic analysis (NPV, IRR, LCOE) to evaluate complex investments under uncertainty.
Experienced leading multidisciplinary research and consulting projects end-to-end — from scoping and proposal development to execution and delivery — and translating rigorous quantitative analysis into strategic recommendations for executives, policymakers, and technical stakeholders.
Originally from Italy, I earned a basketball scholarship to study in the United States, where I began my professional career before relocating back to Milan. Fluent English and Italian speaker.

title: Roberto Vercellino
text:
Work Experience


Researcher III, Quantitative Decision Analysis & Optimization — National Laboratory of the Rockies (NLR), Golden, CO · 2024 – 2026

Center for Integrated Mobility Sciences, National Laboratory of the Rockies (NLR)1, Golden, Colorado, U.S.A.  (2024 – 2026)
Athena Mobility, U.S. Department of Energy, Vehicle Technology Office (2023 – 2026)

Developed transportation demand scenarios and infrastructure models to advise major U.S. airports on decarbonization strategies, informing $100+ million in long-term infrastructure investment decisions and culminating in a briefing to the U.S. Secretary of Energy [1].
Served as primary analytical point-of-contact to executives from 10 of the largest U.S. airports, conducting stakeholder interviews, assessing operational constraints, and identifying cost-effective infrastructure investment opportunities through the Aeroportal.
Developed EVI-Rental, an event-driven Python simulation model estimating costs, infrastructure requirements, and load-flexibility opportunities from EV charging at rental car centers.
Built a parallel HPC workflow to run more than 5,000 Monte Carlo simulations, quantifying tradeoffs between up-front infrastructure investments and decarbonization targets and identifying pathways achieving up to 41% in capital savings [2].

EDGES Microgrid Optimization Model, U.S. Department of Energy (2022 – 2026)

Led technical development of the EDGES decision-support platform for long-term planning of distributed energy resource investments under evolving market, regulatory, and operational conditions [3].
Developed stochastic optimization algorithms (Pyomo, CBC, Gurobi, Ipopt) for real-time economic dispatch and energy arbitrage of distributed energy resources, minimizing lifecycle costs and grid upgrade requirements [4].
Refactored the microgrid design-optimization layer, reducing solution time from 48 hours to 2 hours (24\(\times\)) by testing 5 derivative-free and surrogate-based optimization methods [5].
Delivered investment-focused recommendations across 10+ projects for public-sector and industry clients, translating complex modeling outputs into actionable planning insights.

Data Center Energy Modeling, NLR Strategic Funding (2025 – 2026)

Led a multidisciplinary team of 7 researchers to develop a first-of-its-kind, bottom-up model of AI data center electricity demand, supporting grid infrastructure planning and capacity expansion studies [6].
Directed a team of six in adapting AI benchmark workloads (MLPerf, vLLM) and ran HPC experiments measuring server-level power consumption of re2026ative AI workloads (training, fine-tuning, inference).
Designed and executed reproducible experiments to address critical evidence gaps in AI infrastructure planning, publishing an open dataset and analysis to support industry and policy decision-making [7].

Microgrid EMT Simulation Models, Industry-funded (2025 – 2026)

Scoped, negotiated, and led delivery of an industry-funded project developing MATLAB/Simulink electromagnetic transient (EMT) models capturing sub-second interactions between AI data centers, EV fast charging, and microgrid assets.
Recruited and coordinated a multidisciplinary team of 10 researchers, managed project budgets and deliverables, and maintained ongoing engagement with the sponsoring organization throughout execution.

Grid Impacts of Electrification at U.S. Army Bases, U.S. Department of Defense (2025)

Advised the U.S. Army on fleet electrification investment strategies across three military installations, simulating operation, grid impacts, and costs of five electrification scenarios using vehicle telematics and utilization data.
Integrated stakeholder interviews and sensitivity analysis to identify robust, cost-effective infrastructure pathways. Co-authored findings within a report submitted to the U.S. Congress.

HPC Analytics, NLR Strategic Funding (2025 – 2026)

Supported the ontology design and machine-readable mapping of power flows, telemetry, and control points to enable agentic AI orchestration of NLR’s HPC system.




Researcher II, Quantitative Decision Analysis & Optimization — National Renewable Energy Laboratory (NREL), Golden, CO · 2022 – 2024

Center for Integrated Mobility Sciences, National Renewable Energy Laboratory (NREL), Golden, Colorado, U.S.A.  (2022 – 2024)
Clean Transportation Program (CTP) Benefits Analysis, California Energy Commission (CEC) (2023 – 2024)

Led a 6-person team evaluating the environmental and socioeconomic impacts of more than 1,000 publicly funded transportation projects representing $1.5 billion in investments, supporting future portfolio and funding strategy for the CEC; results presented to CEC Commissioner Monahan [8], [9].
Developed investment evaluation frameworks to quantify environmental and socioeconomic KPIs (e.g., \(\mathrm{CO}_2\) reduced/$ invested) across alternative funding strategies, reducing uncertainty and supporting risk-informed decision-making.
Identified, integrated, and validated relevant data from 20+ NREL, CEC, and public sources; automated the ETL cleaning and processing of 20+ spreadsheets of assumption parameters and project data.

Public Transit Electrification Study, New York Metropolitan Transportation Authority (MTA) (2023 – 2024)

Advised the New York MTA on public transit electrification strategies, simulating operation of an electrified bus depot to evaluate infrastructure requirements, charging loads, projected costs, and impact-mitigation opportunities using onsite battery storage and PV [10].

Microgrid Market Analysis, Industry-funded (2022 – 2025)

Conducted large-scale sensitivity analysis to evaluate how market conditions, policy environments, and technology adoption trends influence the economic value and risk profile of distributed energy investments.
Developed a web application to process and visualize 58,000 U.S. utility tariffs (SQL) from NREL’s Utility Rate Database, enabling stakeholders to identify high-value markets for EV charging, microgrid, and renewable energy investments.




Graduate Research Assistant — Herber Research Group, Colorado State University, Fort Collins, CO · 2020 – 2022

Herber Research Group, Colorado State University, Fort Collins, Colorado, U.S.A.  (2020 – 2022)
FLECCS Project, U.S. Department of Energy, ARPA-E Program

Constructed MATLAB dynamic models of natural gas combined-cycle power plants integrated with carbon capture and thermal energy storage [11].
Implemented nested optimization to jointly determine optimal system design and control, maximizing economic value (NPV, LCOE) through energy arbitrage.
Evaluated the economic performance and \(\mathrm{CO}_2\) emissions of more than 20 technology configurations across hundreds of current and future electricity market scenarios.
Delivered weekly update presentations to the team and contributed to 5 quarterly meetings with ARPA-E.




Laboratory Technician & Data Analysis Assistant — MoVeIT Research Group, University of Torino, Torino, Italy · 2019

MoVeIT Research Group, Medical Physics Department, University of Torino, Torino, Italy  (2019)
MoVeIT Project, Centro Nazionale di Adroterapia Oncologica (CNAO)

Designed and executed experiments (LabVIEW) to evaluate the performance and reliability of prototype instrumentation for hadron (cancer) therapy applications, including noise characterization of a custom ASIC interfaced with a prototype proton sensor.
Performed offline data analysis and curve fitting to quantify measurement uncertainty, assess system performance, and identify key limitations.
